lessons: Long videos: make the first spoken sentence one hard rupee number with a contradiction, like '50 lakh ka ghar, 1 crore ka bill'. Both home-loan videos that opened this way still had 51–52 of 100 viewers at the 5% mark (about 30 seconds). The job-loss video ope

Long videos: bring in the story's person and their problem within the first 30 seconds. All three long videos lost about half their viewers by 5% and about 70% by 10%. In every one, the character (Bhai, Karan, Amit-Neha) only arrives in the second or third sce

Shorts: put a famous name (Sensex, Sahara, Vodafone Idea) in the title and the first three spoken words. Those three Shorts kept 58–78 of 100 viewers at the halfway point. The two without a famous name up front, Shagun and Ketan Parekh/crash, kept 26 and 43.

Shorts: keep the answer to the title's question for the last scene, and end right after it. Sensex SIP went from 56 viewers at 75% to 53 at the end. Shagun fell from 57 to 26 between 25% and 50%, then to just 4 at the end. Length did not explain the difference

Instagram: reuse the Sahara shape, a court or official order plus 'so why is the money still stuck?'. Only 36% swiped away early on that reel, against 55–84% for every other reel, and it got 262 views against 107–135. This is one video, so test it on two more

Label every Short's opening as story picture or presenter. No Short was labelled this week, so the picture-vs-presenter test cannot be read yet. Do not draw rules from UPI (40 views) or License radd (31 views): there are too few views to say.

sglearning.report:
1. Shorts are working: the four with solid numbers kept 45–78% of each video watched, and the Sensex Short kept 53 of every 100 viewers to the very end.
2. Long videos are the problem: about half of viewers leave in the first 30 seconds, and only 3–8 of 100 reach the end.
3. The long videos that opened with a hard number ('50 lakh ka ghar, 1 crore ka bill') kept 52 of 100 at 30 seconds; the one that opened with a 'what if' question kept 35.
4. On Instagram, the Sahara reel stood out: 262 views, and only 36% swiped away in the first seconds, against 55–84% for the others.
5. Videos from Nov 23–26 show 0 YouTube views, so please check they are published or the numbers are still coming in. The picture-vs-presenter test had no labelled videos, so there is no result yet.
6. The one change for this week: start every video with a famous name or a shocking rupee number in the very first sentence

Keep Shorts to about 60 seconds and about 9 scenes. Surpanakha (about 58s, 9 scenes) had 31 of 100 reach the end. Jatayu (about 95s) had 24. Vishnu and Prayagraj Hanuman (about 105s, 12–13 scenes) had only 20 and 15.

Say the hook once, then go straight to the first fact. Every long video and most Shorts repeat the opening question word for word as the first scene line, often after a filler line like 'Ruko, asli khel abhi baaki hai' or 'Aaiye isko samajhte hain'. All three

In long videos, give a first real answer with a named source by scene 2, then open the next question. Ravan–Kaushalya named Ananda Ramayan in scene 2 and kept 14 of 100 at the 25% mark. Chausath Yogini, which spent scene 2 on description, kept 9. Dev Deepawali

arthvan.report:
1) Long videos bring the views (562–897 each), but over half of viewers leave in the first ~40 seconds and only 2–4 in 100 reach the end.
2) Shorts hold much better: 15–31 in 100 finish. The best was Surpanakha: only 38% swiped away early on Instagram and 31 in 100 finished.
3) The weakest was Tulsi–Shaligram: 65% swiped away within 3 seconds, while every other Short we have Instagram numbers for lost 38–50%.
4) Shorter Shorts finished better: about 1 minute gave 31 in 100, while about 1 minute 45 gave 15–20 in 100. Kedarnath dominated the week's top videos (6.9M views).
5) Too early to tell: no video was marked as opening on the picture or the presenter, so that test has nothing to compare yet. Tulsi, Kirtimukha and Hanuman-Ramayan had under 50 YouTube views, too few to judge. Manthara's numbers look broken.
6) The one change this week: start every video with one bold, sourced statement
